caption: The drawing depicts a single large pitcher or ewer, shown in profile, with a tall, rounded, and slightly tapering body that sits on a wide, circular base. The vessel’s body features a smooth, reflective surface with two engraved horizontal bands of intricate geometric and wavy patterns encircling its widest part. The pitcher has a narrow, curved neck that broadens outwards at the spout, which is wide and gracefully extended. The top rim, as well as the bands near the neck, the widest part of the body, and the foot, are decorated with small, repeating rectangular and oval shapes. The handle is long and elegant, starting from just below the spout and rising in a sweeping arc above the vessel before curving down and attaching near the base of the neck; the handle terminates in a small upward curl and displays a leaf-like motif near its upper attachment. The drawing has a monochromatic color scheme, utilizing shades of gray and black with fine cross-hatching and shading to suggest the metallic texture and three-dimensional form of the pitcher. The background is plain and light in tone, emphasizing the central object.
title: Pewter Pitcher
